site.author: Angela St. Cyr
site.about_short: Angela St. Cyr is a home stylist, blogger, and enthusiastic cook based in Vancouver, Canada — one of the most expensive cities in North America. With her two daughters now grown and out in the world of their own, Angela continues to prove that you can live and design the life you want, regardless of budget. Home Stylist, Blogger, Enthusiastic Cook, former participant in the 100-Mile Challenge, and a longtime Jamie Oliver Food Revolution Ambassador.

recipes.title: Sticky Chile Lime Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Sweet, salty, and just enough heat to make your tastebuds hum.

sections.text: I LOVE salads!!! It doesn't matter what time of year, give me an interesting salad with a bold mix of flavours and I'm in! This is one of my all time favourites, it's sweet and salty with just enough heat to get your tastebuds humming. This recipe generously serves 4, allowing for 2 chicken thighs per person.
For the chicken & marinade

items: 8 boneless chicken thighs (skin on or off)
1/4 cup olive oil (lime-infused if you can find it)
Pop everything except the chicken into a blender or food processor and pulse until it becomes a smooth sauce.
Remove 1/4 cup of the sauce and set aside — this will be the base for the salad dressing.
Pour the remaining sauce over the chicken and marinate for at least an hour, or up to overnight.

sections.text: For the salad
While the chicken is marinating, prepare your salad. This is what I like to use, but feel free to swap in anything that suits your taste:
For the dressing

items: 1 tbsp sweet chile sauce (I like Aroy-D)
Whisk everything together in a small bowl.
Season with salt and pepper if needed.
Feel free to add a little more oil or rice vinegar to balance the acidity to your taste.

sections.text: To cook the chicken

items: Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook either in a non-stick skillet or on the barbecue.
Sear one side of the chicken for about 5 minutes.
Flip it over and drizzle 1 tsp of sweet chile sauce over the seared side of each piece.
Cook the other side for 5 minutes, then flip again and drizzle another teaspoon of chile sauce over the second side.
Cook for another few minutes per side until the sauce is sticky and the chicken reads 165°F (75°C) on a meat thermometer.

sections.text: Place the cooked, sliced chicken onto the prepared salad and drizzle with the dressing. This is guaranteed to become a family favourite!
One of my fave easy, healthy breakfasts.

recipes.title: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.description: FOOD This soup just screams fall don't you think?

sections.text: FOOD This soup just screams fall don't you think? It's rich, creamy and hearty enough to keep you satisfied and warm all day. Best of all, this soup gets better and better as it sits so it's the perfect make ahead meal if you've got a busy week.
salt and pepper to taste

items: Cut the squash in half and scoop out the seeds. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Place it on a parchment lined cookie sheet cut side down and bake for 45 minutes or until fork tender. Once the squash is soft, remove from the oven and let cool.

Now all I do is scoop out half of the cooked squash and put it in the blender with the onion, garlic, rosemary and half of the chicken stock. Give it a whiz. Once it's silky smooth I pour it into a medium sized pot on medium low heat. Repeat with the remaining squash and stock.
Once all your pureed squash is in the pot simply stir in the wine and simmer for at least 20 minutes or you can simmer it on low heat for several hours if you'd like.
Turn the heat off and just before serving stir in the remaining ingredients. Season with salt pepper and nutmeg.

recipes.tip:
You could easily pop this into a crock pot on low and just let it simmer away all day. Just remember don't stir in the butter and cream until just before serving.

 This can easily be made vegan by simply swapping out the butter with a vegan butter like Earth Balance and using a bouillon cube like Edward & Sons Not- Chick'n

recipes.title: The Perfect Yorkshires Every Time
recipes.description: I'm not English so I'm not going to pretend that making Yorkshire Puddings is second nature to me, but I will share with you the few tricks I've learned after many years of making some pretty sub-par Yorkshires.

sections.text: I could never understand why sometimes they would turn out like rubbery hockey pucks and other times they'd be as close to perfect as you can get when I was always using the same recipe. So over the years I've researched all the tricks that people swore by and with a little experimenting of my own I've come up with a fool proof method for making these finicky little puffs of heaven.

items: First off you MUST use very good quality free range eggs. I've tried them with regular grocery store eggs a thousand times and I'm never able to get consistent results. I suppose happy chickens make better quality eggs, so I'm more than willing to pay the extra price for them. Always make sure your eggs are room temperature before making this recipe.

My second tip is ALWAYS use full fat milk, I'm assuming there is something in the extra fat of the milk that helps these baby's fluff up to epic heights while still allowing them to be light and crisp.

Another tip is to whiz everything up in your blender. The more air you can get into your batter the better. I give them a good whiz to combine all the ingredients thoroughly, let it sit for about 10 minutes or so and then give them another good whiz.

Now you're going to hate this tip but let the mixture sit in the fridge overnight or for at least a few hours. This seems to be key for consistently perfect Yorkies. Be sure to bring back to room temperature before cooking and give the mixture another whiz in your blender before filling your tins.

For my last tip... be sure to get your shortening or pan drippings piping hot before you pour your batter into your tins. You should hear it sizzle as you pour in the batter. If it doesn't sizzle put your tins back in the oven for a little longer.

sections.text: Now that you have all my tips, here's my recipe

items: Follow all the tips above...don't skip a single one!
Preheat oven to 475 degrees once your batter has come back to room temperature.

Drop 1/2 tsp of shortening or pan drippings into each muffin tin... I like to use shortening because it has a very high smoke point and the Yorkshires stay a pretty golden colour. Place the muffin tin in the oven until the shortening is melted and smoking hot. This usually takes at least 5 minutes.

Now pour enough batter to fill each tin to 3/4. Pop the tins back in the oven and cook for 15-20 minutes. DO NOT OPEN THE DOOR AT ALL DURING THIS TIME. Turn your oven light on after 15 minutes and check to see if they are risen and perfectly browned. If not leave them alone for another 5 minutes.
That's it. If you follow each of these steps you'll have perfect Yorkshires every time!

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH - Strawberry Rhubarb Crumble
recipes.description: It finally feels like spring!!! Any of you living in Vancouver will understand the joy I'm feeling at this moment. It's been a long grey, wet, cold winter and frankly I'm thrilled to see it come to an end.

sections.text: This months MUFFIN OF THE MONTH is a celebration of all things spring. I can't help myself, I always get a little excited when I see local rhubarb and strawberries at the market! It's a sure sign that warmer weather is finally on it's way. Go ahead and give these a try...they are a little taste of the sunshine that will soon be here to stay.
*see rhubarb tip below
grating of fresh nutmeg
Crumble Topping-

items: Toss everything together and give it a good stir. Set aside until you've filled your muffin cups.

sections.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.

In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients and stir in the diced rhubarb and strawberries. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin. Fill lined muffin cups 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop)

items: *If for some reason your muffin mix seems a little dry and stiff feel free to stir in a splash more liquid. Conversley if it ends up a little wet, add a sprinkle more flour. We've always been told baking is an exact science and for many recipes it is, but...I'll never post a recipe like that! All my recipes allow room for a little creative licence and a few corrective measures. So forget what momma always told you lol!
Now simply sprinkle an even portion of crumb topping on each muffin and then pop them in the oven for for 20-25 minutes or until slightly golden.

recipes.tip:
This recipe is easily made gluten free by simply swapping out the flour with a gluten free version such as Robin Hood or my favourite flour blend. You can also make this vegan easily by using an egg replacer.

If you prefer your rhubarb less tart simply sprinkle the diced rhubarb with some sugar and let it sit for a few minutes before adding it into the dry mix.

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH- Marshmallow Hot Chocolate
recipes.description: Well it's December and I'm feeling festive and perhaps a little naughty. Don't tell Santa!

sections.text: Normally my muffins are very healthy, they tend to have little to no added fat, low sugar...bla bla bla. Not this time my friends, it's Christmas so I'm going all out. Fat, sugar and all things yummy! No, these aren't cupcakes, they're still muffins with all their dense moist yumminess, but they are a treat so PLEASE don't eat these every morning for breakfast even though you may want to lol. Merry Christmas everyone. xox
(or 5 packets)

items: * You'll notice I haven't added any sugar. No, it's not a typo...I found the Hot chocolate powder had just the right amount so I decided to delete it.

Line your muffin tins with tulip muffin cups about 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop) when the muffins have about 2 or 3 minutes left carefully place a few mini-marshmallows on each muffin. recipes.title: Chocolate Pecan Pie

sections.text: This is probably my families favourite dessert! Toasting the pecans prior to baking the pie adds such richness and depth while helping to cut the sweetness of the chocolate. My daughter used to HATE pecan pie because she didn't like the jelly-like filling that formed around the pecans. The chocolate cuts down on that immensely, so now she loves Pecan Pie...well mine at least lol. If you try only one pie recipe in your life, this should be it!
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
For the crust

items: 1/3c cold butter or shortening cut into cubes
TIP- If you use half butter and half shortening you'll get the perfect flakiness while still being tender and full of buttery flavour. It's a little more work but it's worth the effort in my opinion.
Pop everything except the water into the bowl of  your stand mixer. Mix on medium speed until the butter pieces are the size of small peas.

Now add 2tbsp of the cold water over the flour mixture and turn the mixer on low speed for a second. If all the flour is moistened and the pastry leaves the side of the bowl then you are finished. It's very important not to over-mix at this point or your crust will be tough. If your pastry isn't coming together yet add another tablespoon or so of water to the mixture and give it another stir. Take a bit of the pastry out and squeeze it. ...if it holds together it's ready, if not add a tiny bit more water and give it a gentle stir.

sections.text: Remove the dough from the mixer, knead it a couple of times and shape it into a flattened round and wrap in plastic wrap. Allow it to chill in the fridge for about 30 minutes. This will make it easier to work with.

items: Remove the dough from the fridge and unwrap it. Place the dough on a lightly floured surface. Using a rolling pin roll the pastry into a circle that's about 2" larger than your pie plate.
Fold the pastry into fourths and place in the pie plate. Unfold the dough and shift into place. Trim any excess pastry so it's 1" bigger than the rim of the pie plate.
Fold and roll the edge of the pastry under and flute the edges simply by pinching with your fingers. Prick the crust all over with a fork, it will help the steam escape while baking.
Set aside until the filling is ready.

sections.text: Filling

items: 1c Rogers Golden syrup or corn syrup
Pop everything except the pecans and the chocolate chips into a large bowl and give it a good whisk. Now stir in the toasted pecans and the chocolate chips.
Pour the filling into your prepared pie crust and cover the edge with a 3" strip of foil to prevent excess browning.

Bake for approximately one hour minutes, removing the foil for the last 15 minutes. You'll know it's ready when it looks all puffy and no longer seems liquid when you give the pan a wiggle. Remove from oven and let it cool for at least  an hour before serving.
I like to serve this with a dollop of vanilla whipped cream. Enjoy!

recipes.tip: I toast my pecans in the oven as soon as it's preheated... just until they become fragrant. It usually takes about 10 minutes or so.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
recipes.description: This is one of my family’s faves! Quick, easy and so delicious.

sections.text: Water

items: **The amount of water you need is dependent on the size and ripeness of your bananas so rather than having a set amount of water I add just enough water to make a thick batter.
This recipe couldn’t be easier! Simply pop all the dry ingredients into a large mixing bowl and give it a whisk.
Then add the wet ingredients and add a splash of water. Give everything a good stir… if it’s too thick add more water, if it’s the consistency of a thick cake batter then you’re  done.
Pour the mixture into a greased loaf pan and bake at 350 degrees F for about an hour or until a toothpick come out clean.
Let cool in the pan for about 15 minutes before tipping it out onto a cooling rack.

sections.text: Enjoy!

recipes.tip: I pop my whole peeled bananas into a ziplock bag then toss all the other wet ingredients into it. Squish it all up until the banana is mashed and the eggs are incorporated. Then I simply squeeze it into my dry ingredients and give it a good stir. Adjust the water as needed. Easy peasy!

recipes.title: Sushi...kind of
recipes.description: In the mood for sushi, but maybe you don't want to spend money eating out? Or perhaps you don't like all the mess when making it yourself? Well I have the best recipe ever!!!!

sections.text: I started making this at home when we used to have Korean home-stay children living with us. It's quick, easy, inexpensive and if I do say so myself, really delicious. All you need is a few packs of roasted seaweed (I get them at my produce market) some sticky rice...or even regular rice that you cook with too much water so it goes sticky. Who would of thought there was a use for improperly cooked rice LOL! Just a few other ingredients and you're done. Quick and easy homemade sushi...who would have thought? See the full recipe below:
several packs                 roasted seaweed

items: Set the seaweed and rice aside.
Mix all the other ingredients together in a bowl and stir.

To serve just let everyone make their own sushi rolls. Simply pick up a sheet of seaweed, add a spoonful of rice, then some tuna and fold in half like a taco. That's it just keep eating them as you make them. It's really a fun social way to eat... my kids love these when they have friends over!

items: Assemble as in the featured picture. If your calories and nutrients allow, feel free to add a second egg. This is one of my FAVOURITE breakfasts!
Get a large pot of water and bring it to a boil, this will be for cooking the noodles.

Now in a small pot pop in the next 10 ingredients and cook covered over medium heat for about 10 minutes or until the chicken thigh is fully cooked. Turn off the heat, remove the chicken breast and dice it up into a similar size as your vegetables and then return it to the pot.

By now the water for the noodles should be boiling so throw the noodles into the pot and cook according to package directions. Once cooked drain them and rinse well with fresh warm water and return the rinsed drained noodles to the pot.
At this point toss the snap peas and the frozen peas into the warm broth mixture and give it a stir. This allows the peas to slightly cook while staying bright green and crisp.
Pour the broth mixture on top of the prepared rice noodles and stir well to combine.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and sesame seeds.

This dish it fantastic warm, but dare I say it’s even better cold! So it’s the perfect make ahead recipe…have it fresh for dinner and then eat it cold as a quick and easy lunch. I eat a single serving for my meal but my husband eats a double quantity and then adjusts his carb intake accordingly for the rest of his meals.

sections.text: I’ve been using the MYFITNESSPAL app for some time now and was only getting pretty depressing results because  my weight was going up and down like a yo-yo. I had only been paying attention the the calories portion and assumed this less than stellar weight loss was because of my age and my inability to do any cardio other than slow walking. At my daughters insistence last week, I started concentrating on the Macros, Nutrients and the Calories portion of the app and I can’t believe the difference…I lost 5.9lbs in one week!!!!!!! I have 28lbs to loose so that’s a phenomenal start and it was substantial enough to keep me encouraged and wanting to learn new recipes and meal plans to keep me on track. I realize most people find this too time consuming in addition to the rest of the things they have to fit into their busy daily routines but I  ABSOLUTELY LOVE doing this kind of thing. So I thought it would be helpful to share my recipes and meal plans with those of you that either don’t have to time or don’t enjoy doing this sort of thing. We all have our strengths so there is no judgement on my part…I’m thrilled to be able to share this with all of you.

items: This recipe is the first MYFITNESSPAL inspired recipe I’ve added to my website, so this section will grow organically over time. I’ll also be sure to share my weight-loss successes and failures with you along the way. It feels so strange for me to be writing about an eating plan to help you loose weight because I absolutely abhor fad diets. I especially hate hearing people talk about them! In all fairness though this is the first time I’ve ever had to actively try to loose weight and it isn’t easy!!!! I’ve always been relatively the same weight and have been very balanced in my eating habits and the amount of daily exercise I get so I’ve never really had to think about it before…not even after I had kids! I left the hospital wearing the clothes I wore before I got pregnant. Feel free to roll your eyes lol.

sections.text: You’re probably thinking what the hell happened all of a sudden that started tipping the scale in the wrong direction! Well I got sick…VERY sick! Long story short I took an antibiotic that has a very rare side effect called Intra Cranial Hypertention which is your body producing too much cerebral spinal fluid which then puts pressure on your brain. The symptoms mimic those of a brain tumour which was VERY scary especially because I have 2 very dear friends that passed away from having brain tumours. After every test known to man and almost a year of seeing several specialists they are 99% sure that is what has happened…it will be confirmed in April after a lumbar puncture…insert scared face here 😳

items: On top of the hell that I’ve been through it’s also had the added bonus of me not being able to exercise or exert myself at all…for several months I could barely even get off the sofa without my brain feeling like it was going to explode. I went from consistently walking between 15,000-20,000 steps a day to 200 steps a day for a 3 month period and now have been able to gradually increase since then. I’m mostly better now but I still can’t do any type of cardio except slow walking, anything more and my head pressure starts up again and I’m out of commission for days.
So that’s my story in a nutshell, feel free to share your stories, weight-loss successes and struggles in the comment section…it’s always nice to feel like we aren’t alone in this.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Lava Cake in Less Than 5 Minutes
recipes.description: What’s a girl to do when she’s craving dessert but doesn’t have anything sweet in the house? And to make matters worse I have one kid that’s gluten intolerant and another that can’t have dairy!

sections.text: Well, they say necessity is the mother of invention and this recipe was created because of exactly that lol. This literally takes me less than five minutes to make from start to finish and I can either make it as a single serving by dividing the recipe by four or I can make 4 servings using the recipe as is and it still only takes 5 minutes…including cooking time! This recipe can be made either gluten free, dairy free or both if necessary. If you don’t have any allergies to consider…go ahead and make this with regular flour and dairy. This really is THE best dessert recipe for a tricky crowd. Are you ready? Here we go….

items: If you’re making this gluten free use a gluten free flour blend, Robin Hood makes a pretty good one and it’s easy to use because it’s already pre-blended. For a dairy free version use a dairy free milk, really any you have on hand will work well in this recipe. Also make sure the chocolate you use is dairy free as well.
Simply mix the dry ingredients together in a bowl and give a quick whisk. Now stir in the wet ingredients and mix until well combined and lump free. Divide equal portions into 4 mason jars or mugs.

Now press a square of chocolate into the centre of each mason jar and then microwave on high for a minute or two. Each microwave is different so keep an eye on it. You want the outside of the cake to look cooked but the centre still to be a bit runny, it will firm up slightly as it cools.
I like to serve this with a scoop of ice cream, some chocolate or caramel drizzle…or both lol…and a few toasted nuts.

sections.text: Enjoy!

recipes.title: Hummus MYFITNESSPAL.com
recipes.description: This is a staple in our house... there is rarely a time when I don't have a fresh batch of Hummus in my fridge.

sections.text: Yes, you can buy pre-made Hummus virtually everywhere these days but you certainly can't beat homemade, especially made my way! I use very little oil and some of the chick pea water to make this Hummus lower in fat and silky smooth. I also have a few other little tricks that add such depth of flavour that this Hummus will be unlike any you've tried before!

items: Drain the chick peas but reserve the liquid. Now pop all the ingredients except the chickpea liquid into your food processor. Turn on your food processor and add just enough of the chickpea water to get it easily moving. It should be the consistency of loose natural peanut butter. Once you have the correct consistency continue to blend until it becomes silky smooth. Feel free to adjust the seasoning at this point, sometimes it needs a little more lemon or even a pinch more salt.

If you'd like to add a little more depth of flavour to your Hummus, why not try adding 1/4tsp cumin or stir in some finely chopped roasted red peppers. You can even make it a little spicy by adding some diced smokey chipotle peppers or a little of the dried powder. There are really endless possibilities to make this your own.
I serve it with a drizzle of olive or sesame oil and a sprinkling of toasted sesame seeds. This stores well in the fridge for at least a week. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Passion Tea Lemonade

items: Simply add the 4 teabags to the boing water and steep until the water is room temperature. Remove tea bags and stir in lemonade powder. Refrigerate until cold.
If you mix this with some vodka or gin it make an amazing martini!

recipes.tip: Instead of the lemon-aid powder you can use the juice of 4 lemons and sugar to taste.
